tei:div.tei:p: O my people! be not silent, and cease not from praying in the place of burnt-sacrifice and offerings made by fire, prepare the appointed supplication as a meat offering offered unto the Lord in righteousness.

The faithful prince of the Lord, the first of my trustful patriarchs,According to tradition Abraham instituted the Morning prayer. rose up early, and prepared his prayers in place of the daily morning offering, and because he believed in the Lord he counted it to him for righteousness. So let it be counted to us when we offer prayers instead of meat-offering!

His only son, with whom he was favoured in his hundredth year, and who was bound on the altar of stones prayed towards evening,According to tradition Isaac instituted the afternoon service. and God graciously accepted his prayer, which he substituted for the evening offering to propitiate his Lord, like the man (the high-priest), who, on the day of atonement, took his hands full of sweet incense beaten small. (So let it be, &c.)So let it be counted to us when we offer prayers instead of meat-offering!

He who dwelt in his tent, and tarried all night in the hallowed spot,According to tradition Jacob instituted the evening prayer, and on the spot where he tarried all night the holy temple was subsequently erected. offered prayers instead of a multitude of pieces of fat, when he approached the slaughter-house, and if at present no sacrifice can be offered, I will prepare hymns of praise instead thereof, for is not to do judgment and justice more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice? (So let it be, &c.)So let it be counted to us when we offer prayers instead of meat-offering!

I am dumb with silence, I am without sacerdotal service, how shall I sing in captivity, when my faithful Levites are taken away; nevertheless I will praise the Lord, who even in judgment sheweth himself sublime; aye, ours is confusion of faces, and to thee belongeth righteousness. (So let it be, &c.)So let it be counted to us when we offer prayers instead of meat-offering!

Let my prayer be considered as a substitute for the fat of the sacrifices, for in praying I remember the order of the service, how the ministering priests entered the inner chambers of the temple, and in the vision heard a voice proclaim, “But unto you that fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise!” (So let it be, &c.)So let it be counted to us when we offer prayers instead of meat-offering!
